images.caption:
Photo of a poster, exhibited near the Warsaw West railway station, Warsaw, 2007

Note at the article Warsaw concentration camp: According to the scheme, a ventilation shaft, which was located closer to the railway station and is seen on the left of the scheme, pumped in air from the outside. In the meantime, hydrogen cyanide gas appearing from Zyklon B was transported by two pipes to the ventilators, where the gas was mixed with air, and then blown into the tunnel via vents in its walls that could be closed. These were the two gas chambers that Trzcińska alleged to have existed. The gas was then pumped out of the gas chambers by the ventilator engines and released in the atmosphere. The scheme says that the Institute of National Remembrance and the Council for the Protection of Struggle and Martyrdom Sites are to blame for the destruction of what is said to be the remnants of the gas chamber infrastructure in 1996.

images.filename: Warsaw ghetto ruins – place of mass executions at 27 Dzielna Street.jpg
images.caption: Ruins of the tenement house at 27 Dzielna Street in former Warsaw Ghetto. This building was located close to the infamous Pawiak prison. After the fall of Warsaw Ghetto Uprising backyard of this house was used by Nazi-German occupants as a place of secret executions. In the years 1943-1944 thousands of Pawiak inmates – Poles and Jews – were murder in this place.

images.filename: 200,000 Poles killed - 200 tys. zamordowanych Polaków KL Warschau.jpg
images.caption: A commemorative plaque purporting that in 1942-1944, 200,000 Poles were killed in KL Warschau (Warsaw concentration camp), as a part of Pabst Plan (which envisaged rebuilding Warsaw as a Nazi model city). The plaque refers to a pseudohistorical concept, according to which said number of Poles were murdered in a giant gas chamber located in the tunnels near Warszawa Zachodnia railway station. There is no evidence such gas chambers existed. According to the vast majority of historians, the total number of killed people is estimated to be an order of magnitude lower than suggested on the plaque.
images.alt: A commemorative plaque purporting that in 1942-1944, 200,000 Poles were killed in KL Warschau (Warsaw concentration camp), as a part of Pabst Plan (which envisaged rebuilding Warsaw as a Nazi model city).
